info.title: KakaoTalk local bridge — serve
info.summary: The HTTP + SSE surface that kanao-cli (Windows) and kamado-cli (macOS) both answer.
info.description:
One contract, two builds. `kanao serve` and `kamado serve` expose the same routes, the same query parameters and defaults, the same request bodies, the same JSON payloads and the same limits; a client written against this document works with either.

What is *not* shared is marked `x-platform` on the member itself: today that is one additive room key (`typeCode`) and one error code (`PERMISSION_REQUIRED`), both macOS-only. `POST /upload`, with the `features` key of `GET /health` that declares it, is answered by both builds since contract 0.22.1 (kanao 0.29.0, kamado 0.27.0). A cut-off notice's whole text — `Notice.truncated`, `fullText`, `fullTextMessageId`, `fullTextSource`, `fullTextTruncated` and `fullTextCandidates` — is answered by both builds since 0.20.0, because both clients cut the notice row at the same 100 characters. The profile pictures added in 0.17.0 — `Room.images` and `Message.senderImage` — are answered by both builds since 0.18.1. The reads added in 0.15.0 are answered by both builds since 0.16.0; where the two clients store less than each other, the route says so in its own description. Anything else differing is a defect in one of the builds rather than a variation this document blesses.

**Every response is an envelope.** Success carries `"ok": true` beside its payload; failure carries `"ok": false` and an `error` object with a machine-readable `code`. The HTTP status and the code say the same thing twice on purpose — the status so a proxy or a `curl` script can branch, the code so a program does not have to guess which of two 503s it got.

**Consumers must ignore keys they do not know.** Adding a key is not a breaking change here; removing one, renaming one, or changing what an existing one means is, and lands in a minor version with the reason in `CHANGELOG.md`. The same applies to error codes: have a default branch, because the two builds' sets are not identical and both may grow.

**Security posture.** A shared bearer token (`--token`, or `KANAO_TOKEN` / `KAMADO_TOKEN`), loopback binding by default, and no TLS of its own. Reach it from another machine over SSH port forwarding, a VPN, or a reverse proxy that terminates TLS — never by binding a wildcard address with a weak token.

**Reads are local.** The server answers from databases the desktop client already wrote; it opens no network connection of its own. Sending drives the client's own window, and `submitted` means the client accepted the text, not that the network delivered it.

servers.description: The host running the KakaoTalk client. Loopback unless deliberately changed.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Is the process up. The one route that needs no token.

tags.name: read
tags.description: Answers built from the local databases. These run concurrently.

tags.name: send
tags.description: The one write. Serialized under a single lock, because the client has one input box.

tags.name: stream
tags.description: Server-Sent Events carrying new messages as the watcher finds them.

get.description: Deliberately unauthenticated: a probe that needs the secret cannot tell a wrong token from a dead process.

features.description: The optional routes this build answers, each with its limits. A route not named here is not answered, and a client must not draw a control for it.

maxBytes.description: Largest file it takes, in bytes. A larger one is refused with `400` before it is read.

get.summary: List the conversations the catalog knows
get.description: Every room in the client's catalog, most recently active first — including the ones whose messages cannot be read, which say so through `readable` rather than being hidden.

get.summary: One room's recent messages, with what they say about attention
get.description: The single call an agent makes to catch up on a conversation: the room, a window of messages oldest-first, who was addressed, and how far the local copy reaches.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many of the newest messages to return. Bounded because `limit` reaches SQLite, where a negative number means *no limit at all* and one observed room holds 445,714 messages.

get.summary: The same window, extracted rather than quoted whole
get.description: Counts, participants, keywords and representative lines per time slice. Nothing is invented and nothing is summarised by a model: a highlight is a message that was really sent, id and all. Measured on one live room, the same newest 400 messages were 116,269 bytes through `/context` and 3,989 through `/digest` — over a link, that gap is the point.

parameters.name: span
parameters.description: How long a slice covers, in minutes or hours such as `30m` or `2h`, at most `12h`. Until 0.21.1 this offered `1d`, which both builds refuse. A span the slicer cannot take is a 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many of the newest messages to consider before slicing.

get.summary: The notice pinned in a room
get.description: Read from the catalog, so it needs no room key and never opens a room. `notice` is null when the room has none. The macOS database has no board table, so its notice is always `source: legacy`.

get.summary: The photos, videos, files and links a room's messages carried
get.description: Looks through the newest `limit` messages and lists what they carried, oldest first. A covered message offers no links while it stays covered.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many of the newest messages to look through.

parameters.name: beforeId
parameters.description: Page backwards from this message id.

get.summary: Every version of an edited message
get.description: Asked only of a message that is still there: one deleted for everyone keeps its history, and reading it back would undo the deletion, so that is `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`. The macOS client keeps no earlier versions at all, so there an edited message answers with an empty list.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id, as a string of digits.

get.description: The copy the client saved when one is still there at the recorded size — on Windows looked for by name in `Documents\카카오톡 받은 파일`, on macOS at the path the client recorded for the save; otherwise fetched from the address, and only from the client's own hosts. An expired address is `410 FILE_EXPIRED` without a request being made.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id, as a string of digits.

Content-Disposition.description: `attachment`, with the name in `filename*` (UTF-8, percent-encoded) and a printable-ASCII fallback in `filename`.

X-Kanao-Source.description: `local` for the client's saved copy, `remote` for the address.

410.description: The file's address has expired and no saved copy was found.

get.summary: New messages as they arrive, as Server-Sent Events
get.description:
Holds the connection open and emits an event per poll. SSE rather than WebSockets because this is a one-way push of small JSON payloads: `curl -N` is a complete client and neither side needs a dependency.

**Resuming is by cursor, not by `Last-Event-ID`.** The stream covers every readable room, so the newest message says nothing about where the *other* rooms had reached — one id resuming all of them would silently skip. After the messages it covers, the server emits `event: cursor` carrying `{roomId: logId}`; hand that back as repeated `since=<roomId>:<logId>` and each named room is paged forward from there before going live. A room the cursor does not name starts from the moment of connection: that is a gap, and it is documented rather than papered over. Fill it with `/context` if it matters.

At most `MAX_STREAMS` (8) connections may be open at once, because each one owns a reader and a watcher for its whole life; the ninth is refused with `503 BUSY` so the eight keep working.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Where to resume each room, as `roomId:logId`. Repeat the parameter once per room.

200.description: The stream. Events are `ready`, `message`, `cursor`, `ping` and `error`; `error` is always last, because the status line is long gone by the time a poll fails.

ping.when: Each poll that found nothing to say.

error.when: Once, and the stream then ends.

post.summary: Send one file through the room's own file button
post.description:
Drives the desktop client the way a person sends a file: on Windows the room's file button, the open-file dialog it shows, and the client's own "파일 전송" confirmation; on macOS the file pasted into the room the way Finder hands one over, then the send button of the confirmation the client shows. Nothing is injected; the client uploads the file itself and shows a picture or video the way it shows one a person sent. The room resolves exactly as `POST /send`'s does, and `openRoom` lets the server open its window.

**Files wait in the same line as texts**: one lock, the same minimum interval, and the same `429 RATE_LIMITED` when the line is full.

**`submitted: true` means the confirmation closed after its send button was pressed**, which is the client taking the file, not delivery: read the room back for a new `fromMe` message. A failure before that button is pressed sends nothing and says so. A confirmation that stays open is closed and answered `500 SEND_FAILED` with an unknown outcome; never retry it without reading the room back.

On Windows the open-file dialog is a real window and holds the keyboard while it is up; the keyboard is handed back afterwards. On macOS the pasteboard is put back afterwards. A file larger than `features.upload.maxBytes` in `GET /health` is refused with `400` before it is read.

200.description: The client's confirmation closed after its send button was pressed.

408.description: The caller promised a body in `Content-Length` and then went quiet, exactly as for `POST /send`.

429.description: The send queue texts and files share is full. Retry once the sends already in line have gone through.

post.summary: Put text in the client's own input box and press Enter
post.description:
The one write in this API. It drives the desktop client rather than any protocol: the room must resolve to exactly one catalog entry, and the client must have that conversation in a window (`openRoom` lets the server open it).

**Sends are serialized and paced.** One lock, and a minimum interval between two of them, because the composer is a single shared resource. A send that arrives early **waits its turn and then goes** — it is not refused. `429 RATE_LIMITED` means the queue itself is full (`MAX_QUEUED_SENDS`, 4, counting the one being sent), which is the only case where refusing is better than a queue that never ends.

**`submitted: true` is queue acceptance, not delivery.** A caller that needs proof reads the room back and looks for a new `fromMe` message. Never retry an uncertain send automatically: the client may have sent it already.

dryRun.summary: Resolve and check without typing anything

openRoom.summary: Let the server open the window first

200.description: The client accepted the text (or, for a dry run, would have).

408.description: The caller promised a body in `Content-Length` and then went quiet. The connection is given up on after `--request-timeout` seconds (30 by default) rather than holding a thread for as long as the caller likes.

429.description: The send queue is full. Retry once the sends already in line have gone through.

error.message: the send queue is full (4 already in line); retry once they have gone through

put.description: `PUT`, `DELETE` and `PATCH` are answered `405` once the token checks out.

bearerAuth.description: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token is ASCII letters, digits or `-._~+/=`, at least 16 characters, and the server refuses to start without one.

RoomId.name: roomId
RoomId.description: The room's identifier, as a string. Ids exceed 2^53, so they cross this boundary as text; a value outside the 64-bit range is a 400 rather than an overflow out of the database driver.

OpenRoom.name: open
OpenRoom.description: Open the room in the client first if its key is not in memory, then answer. Opening a room marks it read in the client, so it happens only when asked; without it such a room answers 503 `KEY_UNAVAILABLE`. `true` or `false` — anything else is a 400, so a typo cannot open a room. Opening is done one at a time, under the same lock as sending. On a host where every room is always readable it changes nothing.

ShowCovered.name: showCovered
ShowCovered.description: Show the text of messages an open chat's SafeBot covered, the way `--show-covered` does on the command line. Off by default, as the client shows them: a covered message carries `covered` and an empty `text`. Asked for, the same messages carry their text and still say `covered`. It applies to this request only. `true` or `false`; anything else is a 400. A message deleted for everyone stays deleted either way.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer token was missing or wrong.

BadRequest.description: The arguments were understood and unusable: a count outside its range, a non-numeric room id, a body that is not JSON, or a span the slicer cannot take. Refused before any database is opened.

NotFound.description: Nothing by that name: no such route, no room with that title, no open window for it, or a window whose input box was not there (`CHAT_NOT_FOUND`, `WINDOW_NOT_FOUND`, `INPUT_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_REQUEST`).

error.message: that room has no open chat window

Ambiguous.description: Several rooms matched. The candidates are attached rather than one being picked.

error.message: multiple catalog rooms share this window title; give the target a unique title

MethodNotAllowed.description: The route exists and the method does not.

ServerFailure.description: The request was fine and this server could not carry it out: a database that would not decrypt or read (`READ_FAILED`), a send the client refused or that could not be verified (`SEND_FAILED`), or a stream asked to resume by a watcher that cannot.

error.message: the catalog could not be read

NotReady.description: The machine is not in a state to answer: the client is closed (`KAKAO_NOT_RUNNING`), it has not opened that room this session so its key is not in memory (`KEY_UNAVAILABLE`; ask again with `open=true`), there is no signed-in profile (`NO_USER_DATA`), the server is shutting down or already holds as many streams as it will (`BUSY`), or — macOS only — the permissions it needs have not been granted (`PERMISSION_REQUIRED`).

error.message: KakaoTalk has not opened that room this session

ErrorCode.description: What went wrong, as something a program can branch on. A consumer must have a default branch: the two builds' sets are not identical and both may grow.

x-code-meanings.KAKAO_NOT_RUNNING: The client is not running or not signed in.
x-code-meanings.NO_USER_DATA: No signed-in profile directory was found.
x-code-meanings.KEY_UNAVAILABLE: The client has not opened that room this session, so its key is not in memory.
x-code-meanings.BUSY: A concurrent write while reading, the stream limit, or a send that was still in line when the server stopped.
x-code-meanings.READ_FAILED: A database could not be read or decrypted.
x-code-meanings.INVALID_REQUEST: The arguments were understood but unusable.
x-code-meanings.WINDOW_NOT_FOUND: The room's chat window is not open in the client.
x-code-meanings.INPUT_NOT_FOUND: The window was found but its input box was not.
x-code-meanings.SEND_FAILED: The client refused, or the write could not be verified. It means "unknown", not "not sent".
x-code-meanings.UNAUTHORIZED: `serve` only: the bearer token was missing or wrong.
x-code-meanings.RATE_LIMITED: `serve` only: the send queue was full. A send that merely arrives early waits its turn instead.
x-code-meanings.PERMISSION_REQUIRED: macOS only: the automation or full-disk permission the client needs has not been granted.
x-code-meanings.MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND: No readable message has that id in that room, or it is not the kind the route asked for.
x-code-meanings.FILE_EXPIRED: The file's address has expired or no longer answers, and no copy saved by the client was found.

x-platform.PERMISSION_REQUIRED: macOS (kamado-cli) only — this code does not exist in the Windows build.

message.description: For a person reading a log. Do not branch on it; branch on `code`.

candidates.description: Attached to `AMBIGUOUS_CHAT`: the rooms that matched, so the caller can choose rather than being guessed at.

Room.description: One conversation as the client's catalog describes it.

id.description: Carried as a string: ids exceed 2^53.

title.description: What this reader composes for the room, which is not always what the client's window is titled.

kind.description: A stable name an agent can branch on. Every client type either build has seen maps to one of these. `channel` (the client's `PlusChat`) comes from the Windows build only: the macOS build decides a room's kind from its shape and has no channel room to name. A type neither build has seen would be passed through as the client's own word, the same string as `type`, so branch with a default rather than rejecting the room. Until 0.19.0 this listed `open`, `plus` and `unknown`, which neither build ever sent, and left out `channel`, `open-group` and `open-direct`, which they do.

type.description: The client's own word for it, passed through.

readable.description: Whether this room's messages can be decrypted right now. A room the client has never opened has no key in memory, and is listed rather than hidden.

typeCode.description: The client's own integer type, passed through without interpretation.
typeCode.x-platform: macOS (kamado-cli) only — absent from the Windows build, and additive, so a consumer must not require it.

images.description: Present only when the room has a picture to draw: the pictures its icon is made of, best first. A room with a photo of its own — one a member set, or an open group chat's link picture — is that photo alone. Otherwise a room with one counterpart (1:1, open 1:1, channel) is that counterpart's profile picture, the chat with oneself is the account's own, and any other room is up to four of its active members other than the account, in the catalog's order. A chat background is not a room's picture. Addresses are HTTPS on the client's CDN (`*.kakaocdn.net`); the cores fetch nothing for them.

Mention.description: One @name, kept as the account it points at rather than as the name. The text carries only a name, and anyone can wear a name; the id is the mention.

name.description: Who that id is *now*, or null when this profile has never seen them.

at.description: Where the name sits in the message text, as the client recorded it.

ReplySource.description: The message a reply was written against, as the reply itself recorded it. This is the client's own copy taken when the reply was sent, so it survives the original being deleted and may disagree with what the original row says now.

Photo.description: Where a picture lives and how large it was sent. Present only on a message that carries one. The client stores an address on its own CDN rather than the picture, so this is the address — the server fetches nothing; a browser can use `url` directly. An album carries its first picture as `url`, how many there are in `count`, and every one of them in `images`. The size is the one the client stored, which a rotated photo can disagree with.

images.description: Every picture the message carried, in order: one for a single photo, one per picture for an album. `url`, `width` and `height` above repeat the first. A size the client did not store is 0.

Video.description: Where a video lives and what the client stored about it. Present only on a video message. There is no thumbnail: across 3,814 videos on the two builds not one attachment carried a thumbnail address, so a viewer that wants a first frame asks the video for it. The address is on the client's CDN and the cores fetch nothing for it. A number the client did not store is 0.

expiresAt.description: Present only when the client stored one: after it the address may no longer answer. Measured at 14 days after the message was sent.

PhotoImage.description: One picture of a message: its address on the client's CDN and the size stored beside it.

Message.description:
One message, already attributed to a named sender.

**The name is the one that account carries now.** The client overwrites its profile tables in place, so a message sent under an old nickname is shown under the new one; `senderId` never changes and is the only safe way to say "same person".

The keys that report being addressed appear **only when they apply**. A window is forty of these, and denying five things per line would triple the answer.

text.description: Empty for kinds that carry no text, such as `feed`, whose stored value is the client's own JSON bookkeeping and is deliberately dropped.

kind.description: The confirmed kinds are named; anything else is left self-describing.

mentionsAll.description: Present only when the message carried an @전체 rather than naming anybody.

mentionsMe.description: Present only when the signed-in account is one of the ids this message named.

reactions.description: Present only when somebody reacted. Who reacted is not stored by the client, only how many chose each kind.

edited.description: Present only when the sender edited the message; `text` is the newest version and `/revisions` lists the others.

covered.description: Present when an open chat's SafeBot covered the message. Its `text` is empty, the way the client hides it, unless the caller asked for covered messages to be shown.

senderImage.description: Present only when the client holds a profile picture for the sender: the small one, HTTPS on the client's CDN (`*.kakaocdn.net`). Like `sender`, it is the picture that account carries now, not the one it had when the message was sent. The cores fetch nothing for it.

Attention.description: The same facts the per-message keys carry, gathered once so a caller can ask "was I addressed" without walking the window.

Coverage.description: How far the local copy reaches, so an empty answer is never mistaken for an empty conversation.

localOnly.description: Always true: this server reads what the client already stored and fetches nothing.

storedLocally.description: How many messages of this room are on this machine. One observed room held 445,714.

messages.description: Oldest first, everywhere in this API.

keywords.description: The client's placeholder words for attachments are filtered out, or they dominate every slice.

highlights.description: Real messages, id and all. Nothing here is generated.

considered.description: How many messages the slicing looked at.

note.description: Says in words that this is extractive: no model ran, and nothing was summarised.

room.description: The room's title, or its id as a string. Must resolve to exactly one catalog room; duplicates are refused with `AMBIGUOUS_CHAT` rather than guessed at.

text.description: What to type. Newlines are allowed.

dryRun.description: Resolve the room and the window, report what would happen, and type nothing. Skips the send queue entirely, so it costs no quota.

openRoom.description: Let the server open the conversation if it has no window, and put the desktop back as it found it afterwards.

submitted.description: The client accepted the text. **Queue acceptance, not delivery** — read the room back and look for a new `fromMe` message before claiming it arrived.

room.description: The window title the text was given to.

clearedDraft.description: An unfinished line was in the box and is now gone. Reported rather than refused, because losing somebody's half-typed sentence silently is the indefensible part.

room.description: The room's title, or its id as a string, exactly as `SendRequest.room`.

file.description: One file. Its part's file name is the name the room sees, reduced to one Windows file name: no folders, none of `<>:"|?*`, no device names, at most 120 characters.

openRoom.description: Let the server open the room's window first, as `SendRequest.openRoom`.

submitted.description: The client's file-send confirmation closed after its send button was pressed. **The client taking the file, not delivery** — read the room back and look for a new `fromMe` message before claiming it arrived.

room.description: The window title the file was sent from.

Cursor.description: Room id to the newest log id the stream has sent for it. Hand it back as repeated `since=<roomId>:<logId>`.

Reaction.description: One kind of 공감 on a message and how many people chose it.

label.description: The word the client shows, such as 사랑 or 엄지척.

code.description: The mini emoticon it is drawn with.

Notice.description: The notice pinned in a room. A board post wins over the older notice row, which in every room holding both was the older of the two.

truncated.description: Present only when `text` stopped at the 100 characters the client keeps of a notice: a board post's preview, or the older notice row, which both clients cut at the same 100. The rest is not in that row; `fullText` says when it was found elsewhere in the room.

fullText.description: Present only when `truncated` and the room holds more of the notice. One source is the post's share (`fullTextSource: share`). It is matched to a board post by the post id, and to a notice row that records no id by its words. Either way the share has to begin with the whole of `text`, so a post edited since it was shared is not answered with its old words. The other source is the one live text or reply message beginning with the whole of `text` (`message`). That message is the notice it was pinned from, and it is **found by its words, not by an id**, which a caller should say. The longer text wins, and equal lengths go to the share. Asked only of a room whose key is already in memory; `/notice` still never opens a room.

fullTextMessageId.description: The id of the message `fullText` was read from — the share or the pinned message. Present exactly when `fullText` is.

fullTextSource.description: Where `fullText` was read from: the board post's share, or the message the notice was pinned from. Present exactly when `fullText` is.

fullTextTruncated.description: Present only beside `fullText`, when its source itself stopped: a share at the 500 characters it carries of a post, or a message at the 3,999 characters the client keeps of a long one. The rest of the post is on the server and the rest of a long message is a file the client did not save, so `fullText` is all a core can read.

fullTextCandidates.description: Present when two or more messages each begin with the whole of `text`: their ids, up to six, and **none is picked** — ambiguity is refused with its candidates.

Attachment.description: Something a message carried. An address, never the thing itself; a file's address stops answering once it expires, and `/file` fetches it.

name.description: A file's name as it was sent; somebody else wrote it.

size.description: Bytes, for a file or a video.

count.description: Present on an album; `url` is its first picture.

revision.description: 0 is the message as first sent.

revisions.description: Oldest first. Empty when the client kept no history for that message.
